Summary: FND-1 Finish client tooling and install dependencies
Description:
**As a** developer **I want** every library, script and dev-server setting in place **so that** feature stories only have to write feature code.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every package from SPEC.md §4 is installed (latest stable).
- [ ] The Vite dev server proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:4000`.
- [ ] Prettier is configured (`singleQuote`, `printWidth: 110`), with `dev`, `build`, `lint`, `format` and `test` scripts.
- [ ] `src/shared/types/api.ts` is a verbatim copy of `server/src/types/api.ts`.
- [ ] `.env.example` contains `VITE_API_URL=/api`.
- [ ] `npm run dev`, `npm run build` and `npm run lint` all work.

## Out of scope
- Using any of the new libraries (that's what later stories do).

**Source:** SPEC.md §4, §8 Phase 1

Summary: FND-2 Align the theme with the design spec
Description:
**As a** user **I want** a consistent, branded look in light and dark mode **so that** the app feels polished and readable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Primary `#5B5BD6`, secondary `#0EA5E9`, and backgrounds light `#F7F7FB`/`#FFFFFF`, dark `#0F1117`/`#171A23`.
- [ ] Inter Variable is the font (Roboto removed). Body is 15 px; h4–h6 use weight 600; code uses the monospace stack.
- [ ] `borderRadius: 10`. Cards are outlined with no shadow. Dialogs have a 16 px radius.
- [ ] Button, TextField, Tooltip and Paper overrides as in SPEC.md §6.1.
- [ ] Text meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes. Theme switching still works with no flash.

## Out of scope
- The Settings → Appearance UI (SET-2).

**Source:** SPEC.md §6.1

Summary: FND-3 Add query client, snackbars and query keys
Description:
**As a** developer **I want** TanStack Query and notistack wired into the app **so that** features can fetch data and show feedback consistently.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `QueryClientProvider` wraps the router, with defaults from SPEC.md §5.5. Devtools render in dev only.
- [ ] `SnackbarProvider` (notistack) is mounted and styled with MUI.
- [ ] `queryKeys` factory exists exactly as in SPEC.md §5.5.

## Out of scope
- Any real query or mutation.

**Source:** SPEC.md §5.5, §8 Phase 2

Summary: FND-4 Add API client, error helpers and session store
Description:
**As a** developer **I want** one typed HTTP client that adds the token, handles 401s and normalizes errors **so that** every feature talks to the API the same way.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An `api` axios instance with `baseURL` from `VITE_API_URL` (default `/api`) adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- [ ] Any 401 except on `/auth/login` clears the session and shows a single "Session expired" snackbar.
- [ ] `getApiError`, `getErrorMessage` and `getFieldErrors` helpers exist.
- [ ] A persisted `auth.store` (key `ai-hub-auth`) has `token`, `user`, `setSession()` and `clearSession()`.

## Out of scope
- Login and register UI, and redirects on 401 (AUTH-1).

**Source:** SPEC.md §3.2, §7.1, §7.2

Summary: FND-5 Build the shared UI kit and format helpers
Description:
**As a** developer **I want** shared empty, error, confirm and avatar components plus number and time formatters **so that** every page handles states the same way.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `ConfirmDialog`, `ProviderAvatar`, `RelativeTime` and `CopyButton` exist in `shared/components`.
- [ ] `formatNumber(12400)` returns `"12.4k"`, `formatNumber(1_200_000)` returns `"1.2M"`, and `formatLatency(1830)` returns `"1.8 s"`.
- [ ] Each component is accessible (labels, tooltips, dialog title) and works in both themes.

## Out of scope
- Feature-specific components (StatusChip, ModelPicker, Markdown).

**Source:** SPEC.md §5.2 components/common, §5.6, §8 Phase 2

Summary: AUTH-1 Sign up, sign in and stay signed in
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to create an account, sign in, stay signed in across reloads and sign out **so that** my provider keys and conversations are mine alone and I always land in the right place.

## Acceptance criteria

### Create an account
- [ ] The form has name, email and password (min 8 chars), validated client side with zod.
- [ ] Server validation errors (`details[]`) show under the matching field.
- [ ] A 409 shows "An account with this email already exists" under email.
- [ ] On success the token is stored and the user goes to `/`.
- [ ] There's a link to the sign-in page.

### Sign in
- [ ] The form has email and password.
- [ ] A 401 shows the server message in an `Alert` above the form.
- [ ] On success, redirect to the `?redirect=` path, or `/`. External redirects (`https://…`, `//…`) go to `/`.

### Protect private routes
- [ ] Signed-out users who visit a private route go to `/login?redirect=<path>`.
- [ ] Signed-in users who visit `/login` or `/register` go to `/`.
- [ ] The 404 page needs no session.

### Stay signed in
- [ ] The token and user are persisted.
- [ ] On app start with a token, `GET /auth/me` runs behind a full-screen loader.
- [ ] A 401 from that call clears the session.
- [ ] The user menu shows the real name, email and initials.

### Expired session
- [ ] **Any** 401 from any API call (except login) clears the session and the query cache.
- [ ] The user is redirected to `/login?redirect=<current path>`.
- [ ] A snackbar says "Session expired", shown once.
- [ ] After signing in, the user returns to that path.

### Sign out
- [ ] "Sign out" in the user menu clears the session and the **whole query cache**, then goes to `/login`.
- [ ] A reusable `useSignOut()` hook is exported for Settings (SET-4).

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.1 AUTH-1 to AUTH-6, §5.4, §9 Auth

Summary: PROV-1 See every supported provider
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to see every provider AI Hub supports and its connection status **so that** I know what I can connect.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A card grid from `GET /providers` (xs 1, sm 2, lg 3 columns).
- [ ] Each card shows a colored avatar, name, description, a status chip (**Connected** green, **Invalid key** red, **Not connected** grey), the masked key, and "Checked 2 min ago".
- [ ] Filter tabs: All / Connected / Not connected.
- [ ] Loading skeletons, an error state with Retry, and an empty state for a filter that matches nothing.
- [ ] Not-connected cards show a **Connect** button (disabled until PROV-2) and a "Get API key ↗" link.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-1, §6.4

Summary: PROV-2 Connect a provider with an API key
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to paste an API key and have it validated **so that** I can use that provider's models.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Connect" opens a dialog with an optional label and the API key (password field with show/hide, placeholder = `keyPlaceholder`), plus a "Get an API key ↗" link.
- [ ] The submit button "Validate & save" shows a spinner (validation takes 0.5–3 s).
- [ ] A 422 `PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED` shows the message **under the key field** and keeps the dialog open.
- [ ] Success closes the dialog and shows the snackbar "<Provider> connected". The card updates.
- [ ] The raw key is never logged, cached or kept after the dialog closes.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-2, §9 Providers & Security

Summary: PROV-3 Test a connection
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to check that a saved key still works **so that** I can fix it before chatting.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Test" calls `POST /connections/:id/test` and shows a spinner while it runs.
- [ ] The result is a snackbar: "Working · 37 models · 412 ms", or the error.
- [ ] The card's status chip and "Checked …" time update.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-3

Summary: PROV-4 Replace a key or rename a connection
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to rename a connection or swap in a new key **so that** I can rotate keys without losing conversations.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The "Edit" dialog has a label and an optional new API key (leave it blank to keep the current key).
- [ ] Same 422 handling as PROV-2 (inline under the key, dialog stays open).
- [ ] Success shows a snackbar and the card updates.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-4

Summary: PROV-5 Remove a connection
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to remove a provider key **so that** AI Hub no longer stores it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A confirm dialog: "Remove OpenAI? Existing conversations stay, but you can't send messages with OpenAI until you reconnect."
- [ ] Confirming calls `DELETE /connections/:id`, shows a snackbar and the card returns to **Not connected**.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-5

Summary: PROV-6 Point new users to the free Mock AI provider
Description:
**As a** new user with no API keys **I want** to know I can try everything for free **so that** I can explore the app right away.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] If the `mock` provider is present, a dismissible info banner shows at the top of `/providers`: "No API key yet? Connect **Mock AI** with any key starting with `mock-` to try everything for free."
- [ ] Dismissing it is remembered across reloads.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.2 PROV-6

Summary: CHAT-7 Browse, search and manage conversations
Description:
**As a** user **I want** my conversation history in the sidebar, with search, pinning, renaming and deleting, **so that** I can find and organize past chats.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sidebar lists real conversations: a **Pinned** section, then the rest by recent activity.
- [ ] A search field, debounced 300 ms, uses `?search=`.
- [ ] Each item shows the title, a provider avatar and a relative time; the active item is highlighted.
- [ ] Its kebab menu has Rename (inline edit), Pin/Unpin and Delete (confirm).
- [ ] Deleting the open conversation navigates to `/chat`.
- [ ] Loading, empty ("No conversations yet") and error states.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-7, §8 Phase 5

Summary: CHAT-14 Open and read a conversation
Description:
> Added story: SPEC.md Phase 5 has this work but no story ID for it.

**As a** user **I want** to open a past conversation and read its messages **so that** I can pick up where I left off.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/chat/:id` loads `GET /conversations/:id` and renders messages oldest first.
- [ ] User messages are right-aligned bubbles (primary at 12 % opacity, plain text, line breaks kept); assistant messages are full width with an avatar and no bubble.
- [ ] Messages with `status: 'error'` render an error `Alert` with the `error` text; `status: 'stopped'` shows a "Stopped" chip.
- [ ] A deleted or unknown id shows a "Conversation not found" state with a "New chat" button.
- [ ] Skeleton while loading; the document title is the conversation title.

**Source:** SPEC.md §6.3, §8 Phase 5

Summary: CHAT-4 Render Markdown and code in answers
Description:
**As a** user **I want** answers rendered as formatted Markdown with highlighted, copyable code **so that** they are easy to read and reuse.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Assistant messages render GitHub-flavored Markdown: tables, lists, and links that open in a new tab.
- [ ] Code blocks are syntax highlighted, with a language label and a **Copy** button, a dark background in both themes, and horizontal scroll.
- [ ] User messages stay plain text with line breaks kept.
- [ ] Raw HTML or `<script>` in a reply shows as text and never runs.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-4, §6.3, §7.5, §9 Security

Summary: CHAT-5 Show model, tokens and latency per answer
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to see which model answered, how many tokens it used and how long it took **so that** I can compare cost and speed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each assistant message has a footer with the provider avatar, model, `↑ in / ↓ out` tokens, latency ("1.8 s") and a Copy button.
- [ ] It shows on hover or focus, and is always visible on touch devices.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-5

Summary: CHAT-13 Pick any model from connected providers
Description:
**As a** user **I want** one searchable model picker grouped by provider **so that** I can choose exactly which model answers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An `Autocomplete` grouped by provider (connected providers only).
- [ ] Options come from `GET /providers/:id/models` for each connected provider.
- [ ] Search matches model name or id.
- [ ] If a provider's model request fails, it falls back to `suggestedModels` and shows a warning icon on that group.
- [ ] The selected value shows the provider avatar and model name.
- [ ] Reusable in Chat, Compare and Settings.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-13, §7.6

Summary: CHAT-8 Switch model mid-conversation
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to switch the model in the middle of a conversation **so that** I can get a second opinion without starting over.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The chat header's model picker sends `PATCH /conversations/:id` `{ providerId, model }`.
- [ ] The next message uses the new model; older messages keep their own model label.
- [ ] The choice persists after a reload.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-8, §6.3

Summary: CHAT-9 Set a system prompt
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to give the model standing instructions for a conversation **so that** every reply follows them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A header button (icon `TuneRounded`) opens a dialog to edit the conversation's system prompt, saved with PATCH.
- [ ] On a new chat, the system prompt is held locally and sent with `POST /conversations` (wired up in CHAT-1).
- [ ] The button shows when a system prompt is active (for example a dot badge).

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-9, §9 Chat

Summary: CHAT-2 Stream answers token by token
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to see the answer appear as it's generated **so that** the chat feels fast and alive.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sending in an existing conversation uses `POST /conversations/:id/messages/stream` (SSE over `fetch`).
- [ ] The user's message appears immediately (optimistic).
- [ ] The assistant bubble shows a typing indicator (three animated dots) until the first delta, then the text grows token by token.
- [ ] When the stream finishes, the final message (with footer) replaces the draft, the title updates, and the conversations list and usage refresh.
- [ ] Pre-flight errors roll back the optimistic message and show an error; a 401 signs out.
- [ ] The stream aborts on unmount or when the conversation changes.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-2, §3.6, §7.3, §7.4

Summary: CHAT-10 Write messages comfortably
Description:
**As a** user **I want** a composer that grows with my text and sends with Enter **so that** writing prompts is quick.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A multiline, auto-growing input (max 8 rows).
- [ ] **Enter** sends and **Shift+Enter** adds a new line. This is configurable via the `enterToSend` preference (when it's off: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends).
- [ ] Send is disabled when the input is empty or while streaming.
- [ ] The hint "AI can make mistakes. Check important info." shows below.
- [ ] Focus returns to the composer after sending.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-10, §5.6 a11y

Summary: CHAT-3 Stop a generating answer
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to stop an answer that's going the wrong way **so that** I don't waste time or tokens.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While streaming, Send becomes a **Stop** button, and `Esc` also stops.
- [ ] Stopping aborts the fetch. The partial answer stays and shows a "Stopped" chip.
- [ ] After a reload the stopped message is still there with its chip (the server saved it).

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-3, §3.6, §7.4 step 5

Summary: CHAT-11 Follow the answer while it streams
Description:
**As a** user **I want** the view to follow a streaming answer unless I scroll up to read **so that** I neither miss text nor get yanked around.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] While streaming, the view stays pinned to the bottom unless the user has scrolled up more than 80 px.
- [ ] When scrolled up, a floating "↓ Jump to latest" button appears and scrolls to the bottom.
- [ ] Opening a conversation starts at the bottom.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-11

Summary: CHAT-1 Start a new chat with any model
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to pick a model and just start typing **so that** a new conversation is one message away.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/chat` shows a new-chat state: a large model picker, and 4 suggestion chips ("Explain a concept", "Write code", "Summarize text", "Brainstorm ideas") that fill the composer.
- [ ] The picker is pre-selected from the `defaultModel` preference, or else the first available model.
- [ ] The system prompt button works locally and its value is sent with `POST /conversations`.
- [ ] The **first** send creates the conversation, streams the answer, and replaces the URL with `/chat/:id` without interrupting the stream.
- [ ] The sidebar shows the new conversation with its auto title.
- [ ] `Ctrl/Cmd+K` opens a new chat.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-1, §7.4 "New chat flow", §9 Chat

Summary: CHAT-6 Recover from failed answers
Description:
**As a** user **I want** failed answers to explain what went wrong and let me retry **so that** one error doesn't derail my conversation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A message with `status: 'error'` renders as an error `Alert` in the thread with its `error` text and a **Retry** button.
- [ ] Retry re-sends the preceding user message's content.
- [ ] `CONNECTION_REQUIRED` (409) shows an alert with a "Connect provider" button that links to `/providers`.
- [ ] Rate-limit (429) messages suggest waiting a moment.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-6, §3.2 error table, §9 Chat

Summary: CHAT-12 Guide me when no provider is connected
Description:
**As a** user with no providers connected **I want** chat to tell me what to do **so that** I'm not stuck in front of a composer that can't work.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] If nothing is connected, `/chat` shows an empty state with a "Connect a provider" CTA instead of the composer.
- [ ] Existing conversations can still be read; their composer shows the CHAT-6 connect alert when sending fails.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.3 CHAT-12

Summary: CMP-1 Set up a model comparison
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to write one prompt and choose up to 4 models **so that** I can compare their answers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/compare` has a prompt textarea, an optional system prompt (collapsible), and 1–4 target rows, each with a model picker.
- [ ] "+ Add model" (hidden at 4) and per-row remove buttons (hidden at 1).
- [ ] "Run" is disabled until there's a prompt and at least 1 target. `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` runs.
- [ ] With no connected providers, show the connect CTA instead.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.4 CMP-1

Summary: CMP-2 See each model's answer as soon as it's ready
Description:
**As a** user **I want** each model's answer to appear as soon as that model finishes **so that** a slow model doesn't hold up the others.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **One** `POST /compare` request **per target** (`targets: [t]`), all sent in parallel.
- [ ] Each card shows a skeleton while loading, then Markdown content, latency, tokens and a Copy button, or an error `Alert`.
- [ ] Running again replaces the previous results. Usage is invalidated after each run.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.4 CMP-2, §5.5

Summary: CMP-3 Compare answers side by side
Description:
**As a** user **I want** answers in a tidy grid **so that** I can scan them side by side.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The cards sit in a responsive grid: 1 column on xs, 2 on md, up to 4 on xl.
- [ ] Every card in a row has the same height and scrolls internally.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.4 CMP-3

Summary: DASH-1 See my usage at a glance
Description:
**As a** user **I want** a greeting and the key numbers on the home page **so that** I know how much I've been using AI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/` shows a greeting ("Good morning, Ada").
- [ ] 4 stat cards: **Connected providers** (x / total), **Requests**, **Input tokens** and **Output tokens** for the selected range.
- [ ] Large numbers are formatted as `12.4k` or `1.2M`.
- [ ] A range selector (7 / 14 / 30 days) drives the numbers. Its state is shared with the chart (DASH-2).
- [ ] Skeletons while loading, an error state with Retry.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.5 DASH-1

Summary: DASH-2 See usage over time
Description:
**As a** user **I want** a daily chart of my activity **so that** I can spot trends.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A bar chart of daily requests, or tokens via a toggle, from `GET /usage?days=`.
- [ ] It follows the 7 / 14 / 30 day range selector.
- [ ] Built with `@mui/x-charts`, readable in both themes, responsive.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.5 DASH-2

Summary: DASH-3 See usage by provider and model
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to see which providers and models I use most **so that** I understand where my tokens go.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "By provider": a list with progress bars in provider colors.
- [ ] "Top models": a table with model, provider, requests, and input/output tokens.
- [ ] Empty states when there's no usage in the range.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.5 DASH-3

Summary: DASH-4 Jump back into recent conversations
Description:
**As a** user **I want** my latest conversations on the home page **so that** I can continue them in one click.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The 5 most recent conversations, each linking to `/chat/:id`.
- [ ] A "Start new chat" button.
- [ ] An empty state when there are none.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.5 DASH-4

Summary: DASH-5 Get started with my first provider
Description:
**As a** new user **I want** the home page to show me the first step **so that** I can get going quickly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With 0 connections, a prominent "Connect your first AI provider" card replaces the charts and links to `/providers`.
- [ ] It mentions the free Mock AI option.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.5 DASH-5, §9 Dashboard

Summary: SET-1 Edit my profile name
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to change my display name **so that** the app greets me correctly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Settings page has a Profile section: an editable name (`PATCH /auth/me`) and a read-only email.
- [ ] Saving shows a spinner and a snackbar; the user menu updates immediately.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.6 SET-1, §9

Summary: SET-2 Choose light, dark or system theme
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to choose the theme in Settings **so that** the app is comfortable to look at.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An Appearance section with Light / Dark / System in a `ToggleButtonGroup`.
- [ ] Applied instantly, persisted, and kept in sync with the user menu's theme options.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.6 SET-2

Summary: SET-3 Set my chat defaults
Description:
**As a** user **I want** to pick my default model and how Enter behaves **so that** every new chat starts the way I like.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A default model picker, used to pre-select the picker on new chats and in Compare.
- [ ] An "Enter to send" switch.
- [ ] Both are stored locally and persist after a reload.

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.6 SET-3

Summary: SET-4 Sign out from Settings
Description:
**As a** user **I want** a sign-out button on the Settings page **so that** I can find it where I expect.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A "Sign out" button at the bottom of the Settings page, with the same behavior as the user menu (AUTH-1).

**Source:** SPEC.md §2.6 SET-4

Summary: QA-1 Polish states, responsiveness and keyboard support
Description:
**As a** user **I want** every screen to handle loading, empty and error cases and to work on any device and from the keyboard **so that** the app feels finished.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every page has loading, empty and error states (SPEC.md §5.6).
- [ ] Every page works at 360, 768 and 1440 px in both themes, with no horizontal page scroll.
- [ ] `useDocumentTitle` on every page ("Chat · AI Hub" or the conversation title).
- [ ] Shortcuts: `Ctrl/Cmd+K` new chat, `Esc` stop, `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` compare. Focus returns to the composer after sending.
- [ ] Every destructive action uses `ConfirmDialog`.

**Source:** SPEC.md §5.6, §6.5, §8 Phase 9

Summary: QA-2 Add automated tests for critical logic
Description:
**As a** developer **I want** tests for the riskiest logic **so that** future changes don't silently break it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vitest + RTL tests for `format.ts`, `errors.ts`, the SSE parser (including an event split across chunks), `LoginPage` validation and `ProviderCard` states.
- [ ] `yarn test` passes with zero warnings.

**Source:** SPEC.md §8 Phase 9

Summary: QA-3 Pass the release checklist
Description:
**As a** team **we want** the full QA checklist, the security checks and performance verified, and a client README written, **so that** v1 is ready to ship.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every item in SPEC.md §9 passes in both themes, on desktop and at 360 px.
- [ ] Security: no raw API key in localStorage, the query cache or the console; raw HTML in replies is not executed.
- [ ] Performance: finished messages don't re-render while streaming; route chunks are lazy.
- [ ] `client/README.md` covers setup, scripts and structure.
- [ ] `yarn lint`, `yarn test` and `yarn build` all succeed with zero warnings.

**Source:** SPEC.md §8 Phase 9, §9
